title: Stock Loss Allowances, Spoilage Credits and Count Frequency by Micro Market Format
content:
Unexplained inventory loss at an Unattended Micro Market Program site is measured against a printed allowance and charged above it at a printed share. Each format also prints how often a full count is taken, how much dated-out fresh stock is credited back before loss is measured, and how long a shrink adjustment may be disputed.

| Market format | Loss absorbed without charge, per cent of sales | Share of the excess invoiced, per cent | Weeks between full counts | Dated-out fresh stock credited back, per cent | Dispute window, calendar days |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cooler & Snack Wall | 1.5 | 100 | 8 | 0 | 14 |
| Compact Micro Market | 2 | 90 | 6 | 50 | 21 |
| Standard Micro Market | 2.5 | 80 | 4 | 75 | 30 |
| Fresh Food Micro Market | 3.25 | 75 | 4 | 100 | 30 |
| Expanded Campus Micro Market | 3.75 | 70 | 2 | 100 | 45 |
| Smart Store Micro Market | 1.25 | 85 | 4 | 85 | 30 |

## How the columns move together

The allowance is widest where the fresh range is widest: the Fresh Food Micro Market absorbs 3.25 per cent of sales and the Expanded Campus Micro Market 3.75 per cent, while the Smart Store Micro Market, at 1.25 per cent, carries the tightest allowance of any format. The share of the excess invoiced moves the other way, from 100 per cent on the Cooler & Snack Wall down to 70 per cent on the Expanded Campus Micro Market.

The spoilage credit is 0 per cent where no fresh line is carried, and reaches 100 per cent on the Fresh Food Micro Market and the Expanded Campus Micro Market. Counts are taken every 8 weeks at the smallest format and every 2 weeks at the largest.
